widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: Can I realise the Self, Maharaj?
sentences: Yes! It amounts to that; unless the individual self is existent how can one realise Ishwara? There is no self, unless the illusion is there. When once the individual realises who he is, the evil effects, i.e., ‘doshas’ of illusion do not affect him. Call it pure illusion, or anything else you like. That is the essential thing.
If you realise your own Reality, then that of the Rishis and Masters will become clear to you. There is only one Master, and that is the Self.
The Self is always directly perceived. There is no moment when it is not so. How then is it to be ascertained? Find out the Self. You are that.
These are also in the mind. They are there because you have identified yourself with the body. If this false identity drops away, ignorance vanishes and Truth is revealed.

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: Does Bhagavan use occult powers to make others realise the Self, or is the mere fact of Bhagavan's Realization enough for that?
sentences: Peace is your natural state.

Yes! It amounts to that; unless the individual self is existent how can one realise Ishwara? There is no self, unless the illusion is there. When once the individual realises who he is, the evil effects, i.e., ‘doshas’ of illusion do not affect him. Call it pure illusion, or anything else you like. That is the essential thing.
Does devotion to Bhagavan mean disturbing other people?
"The intensity of Bhagavan’s direct look is too much for an ordinary human being to take. It is as though some invisible power has entered you and made its way to the very core of your being."

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: How does each body get the life to set it acting?
sentences: The spirit is differentiated from matter and is full of life. The body is animated by it.
The body is only one. Still, how many functions are performed by it? The source of all the functions is only one. It is in the same way with the Gods also.
This corpse of a body does not say 'I'. Even while we are alive, this body is a corpse. It appears so bright and active only on account of the presence of our Self in it.
It is through the same will-power that the seat of all diseases, the body, has risen.

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: Is God apart from the Self?
sentences: To see God is to be God. There is no ‘all’ apart from God for Him to pervade. He alone is

Leave it to Him. Surrender unreservedly. One of two things must be done. Either surrender because you admit your inability and also require a High Power to help you; or investigate into the cause of misery, go into the source and merge into the Self. Either way you will be free from misery. God never forsakes one who has surrendered. Mamekam saranam vraja.
God is no other than the Self
Of course it is. Yet all others and God are not apart from the Self. How can thoughts of them arise when you remain as the Self?

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: If we do not think, do the wars cease?
sentences: Peace is always present. Get rid of the disturbances to Peace. This Peace is the Self. The thoughts are the disturbances. When free from them, you are Infinite Intelligence, i.e., the Self. There is Perfection and Peace.
Yes. That which is to happen will not stop even if we say ‘no’.
Yes - this way. They keep off bad thoughts. They must themselves disappear before the state of Realisation.
Visions and thought-currents are had according to the state of mind. It depends on the individuals and not upon the Universal Presence. Moreover, they are immaterial. What matters is Peace of Mind.
